entries.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.

Asset type: source contact sheet of cooking-step illustrations for the Recipe Nest Vault pho-bo recipe. This is deliberately a sheet for later separate per-step cropping, not a public infographic.

Primary request: create exactly 3 equal columns and 4 equal rows, total 12 equal-sized cells. Canvas must be LANDSCAPE 4:3. Fill only cells 1 through 10, in strict reading order from top left across each row. Keep cells 11, 12 completely blank warm ivory paper; do not omit the blank cells or shorten the grid.

Input image 1 is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its original border-free warm ivory textured paper, fine crisp ink contours, restrained gouache shading and natural food/cookware colours. Do not reproduce the rice preparation subject. No regional palette, ornament, motifs or cultural decoration.

Each cell is a single self-contained step vignette. Entire cookware, food and resting utensils must fit centrally within its own cell, leaving generous paper breathing room on all four sides. Use a consistent slightly elevated three-quarter view, no edge cutoffs and no scene crossing cells. Separate cells only with narrow blank ivory gutters, no frames or ink borders.

Absolute constraints: no humans, hands, fingers, arms, sleeves or body parts anywhere. No text, step numbers, captions, logos, watermark, letters, thermometers with legible numerals, arrows, photorealism or floating utensils. If a action normally needs hands, show the result or a tool resting safely instead. Do not invent finished dishes before their final step. Written recipe facts explain the scene; never draw their words or numbers.

CELL 1 (row 1, column 1): Blanched beef marrow and knuckle bones draining in a colander beside a cleaned large stockpot; pale bones, no finished soup, no people or hands.
Exact written action for context: Cover the bones with cold water in an 8 L pot. Bring to a full boil and boil 10 minutes. Drain carefully, rinse away attached foam, and wash the pot; discard this first liquid.

CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Large stockpot with beef bones and one whole brisket submerged in clear gently simmering broth, lid ajar, a skimmer resting on a saucer, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Return bones to the clean pot with brisket, 4.5 L water, and salt. Bring just to a boil, skim, then leave the lid ajar and simmer at 90–95°C. Plan on 6 hours for the bones; add hot water as needed to keep them submerged.

CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Whole cooked brisket in a shallow dish with a little broth; a wooden skewer rests across the dish edge, bone stock still simmering behind, no hands.
Exact written action for context: After 2½–3 hours, test the brisket: a skewer should enter with little resistance. Lift it into a shallow dish with a little broth. Cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours while the bones continue simmering.

CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): Halved onions and split ginger with browned cut faces in a dry heavy pan, no oil and no black ash, no hands.
Exact written action for context: At the 4-hour mark, heat a dry heavy pan over medium-high. Place the onion halves and ginger cut-side down for 8–12 minutes, turning once, until browned in patches and fragrant. Scrape away loose black flakes and add to the broth.

CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): Toasted star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds and a cracked black cardamom pod in a small skillet beside an open muslin spice pouch, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Toast star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, and cracked cardamom over medium-low for 2 minutes, stirring until fragrant. Tie in a spice bag and simmer with the broth for the final 2 hours; remove sooner if the spice aroma becomes harsh.

CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): Fine sieve resting over a clean pot of clear amber beef broth, spent bones in a separate bowl and a small measuring jug nearby, no hands.
Exact written action for context: After 6 hours total simmering, strain without pressing the solids. Skim excess fat but leave a thin sheen. Measure 3 L broth, topping up with hot water if needed; stir in fish sauce and rock sugar and simmer 5 minutes until dissolved.

CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): Cooked flat white pho noodles draining in one colander and briefly blanched bean sprouts in a separate small sieve, no broth or finished bowl, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Boil noodles in a separate pot for the package time, usually 4–6 minutes, until pliable without a hard centre. Drain and divide among warm bowls. Blanch sprouts in fresh boiling water for 60 seconds, then drain; keep the broth pot free of noodle starch.

CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): Thin cooked brisket slices on a clean board, a separate plate of raw sirloin slices and separate bowls of sliced onion, scallion and herbs, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Slice the chilled brisket 3 mm thick across the grain. Arrange the thin raw sirloin on a separate plate. Wash and dry herbs, slice scallions and the reserved onion, and keep all ready-to-eat garnishes away from the raw-beef board.

CELL 9 (row 3, column 3): Small strainer basket with fully cooked thin beef slices immersed in boiling clear stock, cooked brisket slices visible in the pot, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Bring the seasoned broth to a boil. Reheat brisket in it to 74°C, then poach sirloin in small batches for 30–60 seconds, or longer until fully cooked and 74°C. Transfer meat directly to noodle bowls; do not rely only on hot broth poured over raw beef.

CELL 10 (row 4, column 1): Finished beef pho in a ceramic bowl, flat rice noodles, cooked brisket and thin beef slices in clear amber broth, onion, scallion, herbs and sprouts, lime wedge beside it, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Add sprouts, sliced onion, scallions, cilantro, basil, and black pepper to the noodles and meat. Ladle about 500 ml boiling broth into each bowl. Serve immediately with lime and optional chile; taste the broth before squeezing in lime.

Final layout check: 3 columns x 4 rows, 10 distinct illustrated cooking states, 2 blank cells, all complete and centred. Absolutely no hands or text.

CELL 1 (row 1, column 1): Halved shallots and ginger browning in a dry heavy skillet, warm golden cut faces, no chicken or finished soup, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Pat the chicken dry without rinsing it and refrigerate while preparing the pot. Dry-roast shallots and ginger in a heavy pan over medium-high for 8–10 minutes, turning until the cut faces are deep golden with a few brown patches.

CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Small skillet of lightly toasted star anise, cinnamon and coriander seeds beside a tied spice pouch, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Reduce the pan to medium-low. Toast star anise, cinnamon and coriander seeds for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without scorching. Enclose them in a spice pouch so they can be removed before the chicken flavour is overwhelmed.

CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Whole chicken poaching in pale golden broth with ginger, shallots and spice pouch in a tall stockpot, gentle simmer, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Put chicken, 3 L water, salt, aromatics and spice pouch in a snug 6 L pot. Bring to a boil, skim and lower to a gentle simmer. Cook 35–45 minutes, turning once if not submerged, until both thick breast and thigh reach 74°C without touching bone.

CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): Cooked chicken slices and shreds neatly on one side of a tray, stripped chicken carcass beside it ready for the broth pot, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Lift chicken onto a clean tray and rest 10 minutes. Remove meat with clean utensils and slice or shred into bite-sized pieces. Return bones to the broth. Cover the meat and refrigerate promptly if it will wait more than 30 minutes; remove the spice pouch now.

CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): Clean pot holding strained clear golden chicken broth, fine sieve with chicken bones and softened shallots resting above, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Simmer bones and aromatics for another 45 minutes with the lid ajar. Strain into a clean pot and adjust with hot water to 2.4 L. Stir in fish sauce and simmer 2 minutes; the broth should taste savoury and gently aromatic, not strongly of cinnamon.

CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): Drained flat rice noodles in a colander, sliced onion and scallion greens in small bowls, clean cilantro and lime wedges on a board, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Cook noodles separately for the package time, usually 4–6 minutes, until supple with no hard centre; drain. Thinly slice scallion greens and onion, wash and dry cilantro, and cut lime. Blanch scallion whites in the broth for 30 seconds.

CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): Cooked sliced chicken being reheated in a small strainer resting in pale golden broth, no raw meat, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Bring broth back to a simmer and submerge the sliced chicken for 1–3 minutes, or until it reaches 74°C. Use a strainer to lift it out as soon as hot so the breast stays tender. Divide noodles among four warm bowls.

CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): Finished chicken pho with pale cooked chicken slices, flat white noodles, clear golden broth, scallion, onion and cilantro, lime on the side, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Top noodles with chicken, scallion whites and greens, onion, cilantro and black pepper. Bring broth just to a boil and pour about 600 ml into each bowl. Serve immediately with lime and optional chile, hoisin and Sriracha served separately.

Final layout check: 3 columns x 3 rows, 8 distinct illustrated cooking states, 1 blank cells, all complete and centred. Absolutely no hands or text.

Exact written action for context: Cover beef bones, shank and pork hock with cold water in an 8 L pot. Bring to a boil for 5 minutes, drain, and rinse off foam. Clean the pot before making the broth.

CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Large pot of clear beef and pork broth with long bruised lemongrass stalks and onion halves, lid ajar, no red oil yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Return the meat and bones with 4 L water, onion, bruised lemongrass and salt. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently with the lid ajar for 3–3½ hours, removing each meat when tender. Top up with hot water to keep bones covered.

CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Tender pale pork hock pieces with intact skin and bones in a shallow bowl with a little broth, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Check pork hock after 75–90 minutes: skin should yield easily to a skewer but still hold together. Transfer to a shallow container with some broth. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours while the beef and bones continue cooking.

CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): Small bowl of diluted fermented shrimp paste settling beside a clear spoon and cup of hot broth, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Mix shrimp paste with 100 ml hot broth drawn from the pot. Stir until no dense lumps remain, then leave 5 minutes. Use the smooth upper liquid and leave any gritty sediment behind.

CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): Small saucepan of clear red-orange annatto oil beside a sieve holding spent annatto seeds, no chile or garlic added yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Heat oil and annatto seeds in a small pan over medium-low for 2–3 minutes until the oil turns red-orange. Do not let the seeds smoke. Strain into a heatproof bowl and discard the seeds, then return the oil to the pan.

CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): Finely minced lemongrass, shallot and garlic simmering in red chile-annatto oil in a small skillet, thick aromatic paste, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Add shallots, garlic and minced lemongrass to the annatto oil. Cook over medium-low for 4–5 minutes until fragrant and softened. Stir in chile flakes for 30 seconds, then add diluted shrimp paste and cook 1 minute. Scrape this mixture into the broth.

CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): Tender whole cooked beef shank resting on a board beside a pot of red-orange lemongrass broth, bones and long stalks removed, no hands.
Exact written action for context: When shank is easily pierced after 3–3½ hours, remove it and rest 15 minutes. Discard bones, onion and long lemongrass stalks. Adjust broth to 3 L with hot water; add fish sauce and sugar and simmer 5 minutes, keeping the fine red aromatics in the soup.

CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): Thick round white rice noodles draining in a colander, a single curved noodle visible to show round cross-section, no flat pho noodles, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Boil noodles in a separate large pot for their package time, typically 12–15 minutes. Bite one to check that the white hard centre is gone but the noodle remains springy. Rinse briefly with warm water and drain thoroughly.

CELL 9 (row 3, column 3): Side platter of finely shredded purple cabbage, blanched sprouts, red onion, mint, basil and lime wedges, no soup or hands.
Exact written action for context: Blanch sprouts in boiling water for 60 seconds and drain. Wash and dry shredded cabbage and herbs. Arrange with thin red onion and lime wedges. Keep the herbs out of the stockpot so their fresh aroma survives serving.

CELL 10 (row 4, column 1): Slices of cooked beef shank and intact pork hock pieces reheating in red-orange broth, no noodles yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Slice beef shank across the grain into 3 mm slices. Return beef and chilled pork hock to the simmering broth for 3–5 minutes, or until both reach 74°C. Keep pork pieces intact and remove any loose bones before serving.

CELL 11 (row 4, column 2): Finished bun bo Hue bowl with thick round noodles, sliced beef shank and bone-in pork hock in red-orange broth, scallion and cilantro, cabbage and herb plate beside, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Divide noodles and hot meats among six bowls. Ladle about 500 ml broth into each, including a little red aromatic oil. Add scallions and cilantro; serve the vegetables and lime alongside so each diner can add crunch and acidity.

Final layout check: 3 columns x 4 rows, 11 distinct illustrated cooking states, 1 blank cells, all complete and centred. Absolutely no hands or text.

CELL 1 (row 1, column 1): Clean blanched short pork rib pieces in a colander beside an empty clean stockpot, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Cover ribs with cold water, bring to a boil and boil 5 minutes. Drain, rinse away foam and bone fragments, and wash the pot. This blanching water is discarded rather than used for the tomato broth.

CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Pork rib stock gently simmering in a pot, pale broth and tender rib pieces, lid ajar, no tomatoes yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Add ribs, 2.5 L fresh water and salt to the clean pot. Bring to a boil, skim, and simmer gently with the lid ajar for 75 minutes until the ribs are tender. Keep the ribs for serving and adjust the liquid to 2 L with hot water.

CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Tomato wedges softening with minced shallots and garlic in a skillet, orange-red juices collecting but wedges intact, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Heat oil over medium in a frying pan. Cook 60 g shallots and all garlic for 2 minutes until fragrant, then add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, turning gently. The cut edges should soften while the wedges still keep their shape; scrape everything into the stock.

CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): Mixing bowl of soft chunky crab, minced shrimp, pork and beaten egg mixture with minced shallot, spoon resting inside, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Mix crab, minced shrimp, ground pork, eggs, remaining 20 g shallots, 10 ml fish sauce and pepper until evenly combined. Keep the mixture cold. It should be soft and spoonable, not kneaded into a smooth, rubbery paste.

CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): Rustic pale crab-pork dumplings setting on the surface of gently simmering tomato broth, no stirring utensil in motion and no hands.
Exact written action for context: Bring tomato broth to a steady simmer. Lower 16 heaped spoonfuls of crab mixture into it, keeping each about 4 cm wide. Do not stir for the first 5 minutes. Simmer 15–18 minutes until firm enough to lift and the centre of the largest dumpling reaches 74°C.

CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): Golden fried tofu cubes nestled between crab dumplings and tomato wedges in red-orange soup, no noodles yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Dilute shrimp paste in 60 ml hot broth, then add with the remaining 25 ml fish sauce and sugar. Slip tofu between the dumplings and simmer 5 minutes until hot throughout. Stir around the edge gently so the delicate crab pieces remain intact.

CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): Fine round rice vermicelli draining in a colander beside four empty deep bowls, no finished soup, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Cook rice vermicelli separately according to its package, usually 5–7 minutes in boiling water. Taste for a tender centre, then rinse briefly under warm water and drain well. Divide among four deep bowls without adding the starchy cooking water to the soup.

CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): Fresh platter with blanched bean sprouts, mint, perilla, cilantro, lime wedges and sliced chile, small dish of scallions, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Blanch sprouts in fresh boiling water for 60 seconds and drain. Wash and dry herb leaves, slice scallions, and cut the lime and optional chile. Keep these on a clean platter separate from any utensils used for raw dumpling mixture.

CELL 9 (row 3, column 3): Finished bun rieu with fine round noodles, rustic crab dumplings, tomato wedges, fried tofu and pork ribs in red tomato broth, herbs and lime on the side, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Top each noodle bowl with four crab dumplings, pork ribs, tofu and tomato wedges. Ladle hot broth gently around them and scatter scallions. Serve immediately with sprouts, herbs, lime and optional chile; add lime at the table to retain its fresh aroma.

CELL 1 (row 1, column 1): Small saucepan of amber caramel syrup cooling on a trivet, measured water jug nearby, no meat yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Heat 25 g sugar with 20 ml water in a small pan over medium for 5–7 minutes until amber. Remove from heat and carefully add the remaining 30 ml of the caramel water; it will bubble. Swirl and cool 10 minutes before mixing with pork.

CELL 2 (row 1, column 2): Bowl of seasoned ground pork flecked with finely minced shallot and lemongrass under a loose cover, no formed patties yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Combine pork, cooled caramel, 30 ml fish sauce, oyster sauce, shallots, 15 g garlic, lemongrass and pepper. Mix just until sticky and evenly seasoned, about 1 minute. Cover and refrigerate at 4°C or below for 1 hour; prepare pickles during this wait.

CELL 3 (row 1, column 3): Thin small slices of pale green papaya and orange carrot submerged in clear quick-pickling liquid in a glass bowl, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Toss papaya and carrot with salt for 10 minutes, then rinse and drain well. Dissolve 15 g sugar in 100 ml water and vinegar. Add vegetables and refrigerate at least 30 minutes until crisp and lightly sour; drain before serving.

CELL 4 (row 2, column 1): Clear pale amber dipping sauce with minced garlic and red chile in a bowl, small jug beside, no meat yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Warm the remaining 350 ml water and dissolve the remaining 40 g sugar. Cool until lukewarm, then stir in 50 ml fish sauce, lime juice, remaining 10 g garlic and optional chile. The sauce should be light enough to dip noodles, not as salty as straight fish sauce.

CELL 5 (row 2, column 2): Plate of drained thin rice vermicelli beside a platter of dry lettuce, mint, cilantro and perilla, no pork yet, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Boil vermicelli according to its package, usually 5–7 minutes, until no hard centre remains. Rinse with cool potable water and drain for 5 minutes. Arrange noodles, washed dry lettuce and herbs on separate serving plates.

CELL 6 (row 2, column 3): Sixteen small raw pork patties arranged on a tray, uniform round flattened shape and flecks of aromatics, grill pan warming nearby, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Divide the chilled pork evenly into 16 portions. Shape into patties about 6 cm wide and 2 cm thick. Keep them cool while a lightly oiled grill pan heats over medium-high for 3 minutes.

CELL 7 (row 3, column 1): Pork patties on a ridged grill pan with dark caramelized grill marks and lightly charred edges, no raw centre visible and no hands.
Exact written action for context: Grill patties in two uncrowded batches over medium to medium-high, 4–5 minutes per side. Turn only when the underside releases easily. Check the thickest centre reaches 71°C; if the surface darkens early, reduce heat and continue until safe inside.

CELL 8 (row 3, column 2): Four already-cooked Vietnamese fried spring rolls crisping on a wire rack over a baking tray, golden bubbled rice-paper skins, no hands.
Exact written action for context: If serving cooked chả giò, re-crisp four rolls on a rack in a 190°C oven for 8–12 minutes, until crisp and the centre reaches 74°C. Follow the producer's longer time if required. This step uses fully cooked rolls, not raw frozen rolls.

CELL 9 (row 3, column 3): Finished Hanoi bun cha: grilled pork patties and thin papaya-carrot pickles in a small bowl of clear amber dipping sauce, a separate plate of rice vermicelli and fresh herbs, optional fried roll on side, no hands.
Exact written action for context: Divide patties and drained pickles among four small deep bowls and add the light dipping broth. Serve warm pork with noodles, lettuce and herbs alongside, plus one optional fried roll per person. Dip a little noodle and herb into the sauce with each bite.

Final layout check: 3 columns x 3 rows, 9 distinct illustrated cooking states, 0 blank cells, all complete and centred. Absolutely no hands or text.
